Cál ceannann: Colcannon

Well did you ever make colcannon
made with lovely pickled cream
with the greens and scallions mingled
like the picture in the dream.
Did you ever make a hole on top
to hold the meltin’ flake
of the creamy-flavoured butter
that our mother used to make?

Oh you did, so you did,
so did he and so did I.
And the more I think about it, sure
the nearer I’m to cry.
Oh weren’t them the happy days
when troubles we knew not
and our mothers made colcannon
in the little skillet pot.

Well did you ever take potato cake
and boxty to the school
tucked underneath your oxter
with your books, your slate and rule?
And when teacher wasn’t lookin’,
sure, a great big bite you’d take
of the creamy-flavoured soft
and meltin’ sweet potato cake.

Well did you ever go a-courtin’ boys
when the evenin’ sun went down
and the moon began apeepin’
from behind the Hill o’ down.
Did you wandered down the boreen
where the clúrachán was seen
and you whispered lovin’ praises
to your own dear sweet colleen.

↳ Posted by dancingfiddle@gmail.com on March 28th, 2018.

Re: The First Of May

The words of the song ‘The little skillet pot’ were written by Shaun O’Nolan, storyteller, actor, songwriter and uilleann piper from Barraderry, Kiltegan, County Wicklow. He was born John Nolan in 1872 and emigrated to Boston in 1903. He styled himself as ‘The Wicklow Piper’. More information is available on the ‘Lives of the Pipers’ website:
http://livesofthepipers.com/1o’nolanshaun.html

The tune is older and appears in ‘Anderson’s Fifty New Scottish and Irish Reels and Hornpipes’, published in Scotland in 1826 as “Lady Harrington’s Reel.” More information is on the Traditional Tune Archive website.

It is also included in Canon Goodman’s Collection of music made in Co. Kerry in the mid-19th century (vol 2. p 159). It is not included in the two published volumes from the Irish Traditional Music Archive but the original hand-written score can be viewed on line at the ITMA web site. Interestingly no C sharps are indicated but possibly this is an omission:
http://goodman.itma.ie/volume-two#?c=0&m=0&s=0&cv=162&z=-4813.5288%2C0%2C17803.0576%2C6432
